steps.content: What? Someone took Deren away?
Who? Who took her away without my permission?
In the past few days, you've been studying Deren's notebook, justifying it as a way of better understanding one of your Sinners.
This is the last thing you want to hear—that one of your Sinners has been taken away without your permission, when you've just arrived at work sleep-deprived and bleary-eyed.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: A councilor from Eastside asked for her. That is a very high ranking official, higher than you, Chief. So... we couldn't stop it.

steps.speaker: Nightingale
steps.content: And... Sinner MBCC-S-014 counts as one of the "Elite Sinners", thus is entitled to temporary release from detention.
Nightingale gives you an apologetic smile and hands you the terminal she's holding.
A live interview is being shown on the screen. The miniature image of a burning fire next to the title indicates that the interview has drawn a large audience.

steps.speaker: Reporter A
steps.content: Miss Deren, it's been some time since your last appearance at a DisCars ceremony. Could you tell us why you've decided to come back?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: They invited me, so I came.

steps.speaker: Reporter A
steps.content: Do you have anything to say about the ceremony being delayed?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: It's delayed, not canceled.

steps.speaker: Reporter B
steps.content: Is it true that you didn't submit a movie for consideration this time?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: It's true. Because I haven't made any.

steps.speaker: Reporter B
steps.content: Why? We like your movies. They are refreshing, a mixture of romance and absurdness.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Why haven't I made any new movies? Haha... Haven't got around to it, I guess.

steps.speaker: Reporter C
steps.content: Are you happy with your old movies?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: What's important is whether you're happy with them.

steps.speaker: Reporter C
steps.content: What do you think about the title "the Queen of Absurdness"?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I'm no queen of any kind. I'm just a director who makes movies she enjoys making.

steps.speaker: Reporter D
steps.content: Miss Deren, I have a question for you...

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Ask away.

steps.speaker: Reporter D
steps.content: You've been out of the public eye for five years. Have you been collecting material for a movie?

steps.speaker: Reporter E
steps.content: You've finally agreed to attend the DisCars ceremony, and it's been delayed due to a singular event. Could you share your view on this event? Are you considering turning it into a movie?

steps.speaker: Reporter F
steps.content: Do you plan to attend future DisCars ceremonies?

steps.speaker: Reporter
steps.content: Miss Deren, would you please answer my question? Miss Deren...

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Whoa, whoa... Slow down! One at a time...
Deren maintains her smile. She squints her eyes to face the passionate crowd.
An array of microphones, like fearsome truncheons, are stuck up close to Deren's face, each carrying a nameplate.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I'll answer your questions as best I can.
Deren is cornered. There seems no hope of escape.
Deren sighs and takes small steps backward.

steps.speaker: Reporter
steps.content: You sighed, because you feel the film industry is hopeless?

steps.speaker: Reporter
steps.content: Is this the reason why you went into hiding for so long?

steps.speaker: Reporter
steps.content: You've come out of hiding, because you want to bring the film industry back to life?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Haha... I'm flattered that you think I can pull off such a feat.
Deren's face grows solemn, as inexplicable emotions churn inside her. Something deep in her psyche seems to be stirring, threatening to break free of the restraints her rationality puts on it.
Don't be tempted.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Who?
On the count of three, turn around and run southwest.
With the familiar voice reverberating in her head, Deren smiles, raises her head, and speaks into the bank of microphones.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Sorry, but I have to digress a little. I have an announcement to make.
One...

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Which is...
Two...

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: How should I put it...
Three...

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I'm off. See ya!

One minute she was scratching her head, pretending to search for words. The next she was off like a runaway horse, avoiding street signs and roadblocks as she goes. Shortly, she disappeared without a trace.
Silence descends on the crowd of reporters, but it is short-lived, presently replaced by an uproar.

steps.speaker: Reporters
steps.content: Why is she running away?

steps.speaker: Reporters
steps.content: Is she off to save the film industry?

steps.speaker: Reporters
steps.content: I don't think so. I think what she is trying to say is that no one can touch her in this profession.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Chief, are you experiencing a feeling of déjà vu?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Or a flashback, like in a movie.
Taking Deren by the hand, you dash around in a maze of narrow alleys, and finally slow down when you have lost the reporters and bodyguards.
Are you saying I'm the star of a movie?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Of course. You'll always be the star of my eyes.
Then please tell me how to "act" right now, Director Deren, because I have a bellyful of questions.
You lead Deren into a narrow cul-de-sac that ends in a high wall.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Oh my, why get so serious all of a sudden?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I'll answer your questions honestly. I'm not gonna mess with you, as I did with those boring idiots.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: You.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Just kidding... I know you're asking who took me away from the MBCC.
Deren leans against the wall, arms crossed. Specks of dust alight on her shoulders. It brings to mind the image of a long-forgotten wooden box collecting dust in a dark corner.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: It's an old friend, he is...

steps.speaker: Ringtone
steps.content: Beep,beep.
A shrill ringing of the phone interrupts Deren. She fishes out her communicator, takes a look at the screen—her assistant is calling her, and gives you a sheepish smile.
Deren answers the phone. A penetrating voice comes through.

steps.speaker: Assistant
steps.content: Good Lord, what have you done! How could you run away in the middle of an interview?

steps.speaker: Assistant
steps.content: Do I have to remind you who got you out of the MBCC? I guess I have to. It's Councilor Walter!

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I know, I know... But he said that as long as I showed up, I could say as I pleased, and do as I pleased.

steps.speaker: Assistant
steps.content: Didn't you work with him before? Why would you put him in an awkward position? Don't you know he holds sway in the business world and on the political scene?

steps.speaker: Assistant
steps.content: He's the one who financed this DisCars ceremony. You'd better not get in his bad books, or he...
Deren jerks her head away from the communicator. She furrows her brow and jams a finger in her ear.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Okay, okay... I'll listen to you. I'll attend the ceremony. I promise.
Having put her angry assistant's mind at ease, Deren turns off the communicator.
For a moment, it seems that the brick alley is buzzing as the assistant's voice fades away.
So... if you don't give interviews, or attend the ceremony...
He'll pull out?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I guess so. You heard my assistant.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I've long since lost interest in that kind of stuff, but I know...

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: A lot of people depend on that for their livelihood, and it's not gonna cost me anything, right? So, I'll go and do their bidding.
So... that movie of yours, did you agree to have it edited by someone else, because you didn't want people to lose their jobs?
Deren is struck dumb by your words for a moment, but then roars with laughter.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Haha... You sure are different. Did you pick up something?
You shrug and motion for her to follow you.
You leave the alley and soon arrive at a factory, from within which noises come gushing.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: What is this place?
Deren seems confused, looking around.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: So, this is my punishment for leaving the MBCC without saying goodbye to you, to be thrown into a factory to do hard labor?
Now I understand why you could win the best director award.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Enough with the praising. I'm getting tired of it.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Why did you bring me here anyway?
You show Deren the notebook you found the other day.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Looks like you've done your research.
You're my Sinner now, and as Chief of the MBCC, it's my responsibility to...
Have a thorough understanding... of each and every one of my Sinners.
Deren narrows her eyes at you, incredulous.
You open the notebook and read from it.
"The dancers behind the door, they tried bravely, they struggled sadly, but in the end, they accepted their fate."
"Maybe it's because they felt helpless, maybe there's no reason at all, or maybe it's because they didn't care anymore."
"But little did they know the cost of accepting their fate was destruction."
"Then... who should cry out for the voices they hide in their hearts?"

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Oh my, it's embarrassing to hear my stuff being read out loud by someone else.
The movie Luvia showed me... it's been so heavily edited that it feels off to me.
But, no matter how deceiving editing techniques can be, the director's true intentions are always revealed in the eyes of the actors.
You left this notebook for me on purpose, didn't you?

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I just wanted to see how much you could discover. I have a feeling that you've discovered more than I expected.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Chief of the MBCC, you're really something.
You pass Deren the notebook, and she takes it. She runs her hand over the cover, looking as if she is connecting with her younger self.
Those labels that the internet and media desperately try to put on you are not who you really are. They are just, labels.
They don't define you or your movies.
The movie you wanted to show the world is not a romance movie, or one of those feel-good movies.
It's a profound movie intended for the audience to hear the cry of those who break the bonds of fate.
Unfortunately, the movie, like the director, is unfairly labeled. It's been altered, and its message has been distorted.
The boom of machinery shutting down issues from behind the closed gate of the factory, lingering in the air between the silent Deren and you.
The gate opens, unleashing a wave of workers. The two of you, standing among the moving crowd, are like two drops in the ocean.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: What you just said is all true. But... it is what it is.
Now there is a steady stream of workers that separates you from Deren. She gives you a childlike smile, just like the one she gave you in your first encounter.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: Making movies takes money. My movie was no exception; a lot of people invested in it.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I did want the world to see my movie, to see my ideas being realized on the screen.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: But you can't always get what you want. If it was the director's cut that had been used, it would've never been accepted, and the efforts of everyone involved in making the movie would've gone down the drain.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I couldn't let that happen.
The sun has set low, and the temperature has dropped. Thin clouds form as you breathe.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: The movie won universal acclaim after it was screened in the DisCars. Everyone was celebrating.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I'm the only one who was angry. I wasn't angry with them, because they hadn't done anything wrong.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I guess... I was angry with myself.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I was angry, and tried and failed to justify to myself what I had done. Then in my chaotic mind, something exploded into existence and split into many shadows—fifty of them, maybe. They took over my mind and started dancing.
Deren opens her arms and starts twirling like the dancers in the movie, making a full circle around you.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: The dance was replayed over and over in my mind. And over and over, the shadow figures died before my eyes.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I wanted to do something for them, so I shot some short films and got on talk shows that I had previously avoided.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: But what I said on the talk shows and through my short films was nothing more than a drop of water in the ocean, vanished without a trace.
Deren is standing with her back to you. You can't see her expression, but you can hear the helplessness and frustration in her voice.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: So... that's that.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: I accepted reality. That's not the end of the world.

steps.speaker: Deren
steps.content: They sold out, they partied... As for me, I stopped making movies. What I earned is enough to last me a lifetime.
You're looking at Deren's back. As she delivers the last remark, she shrugs slightly, and perhaps... proudly.
You step forward to stand beside her. When you speak again, your tone of voice is strangely detached, just like Deren's.
Accepting reality... Doesn't it mean you can't change it? Doesn't it mean you can only sit by and do nothing?
